title: LSASS memory access with full-access mask by PowerShell on scranton (and wsmprovhost on nashua)
rationale: All describe the same LSASS handle-open events: PowerShell PID 2976 on scranton with 0x1f3fff/0x1fffff and UNKNOWN call trace, plus wsmprovhost.exe on nashua with 0x1f3fff. F23/F32/F36 add the steganographic loader context for the same PID 2976 event; F52 notes the same precursor with no web-credential forging. Best fit: OS Credential Dumping - LSASS Memory.

title: NASHUA: python.exe via PsExec opened LSASS, read LSA secrets, staged credential archive
rationale: LSASS 0x1f3fff access plus LSA registry reads and credential archive staging on nashua. Best fit LSASS Memory.

title: Cached domain credential registry writes by lsass (benign logon caching)
rationale: NL$1 writes by lsass align with PsExec logons; assessed as caching, not cachedump. Best-fit technique is Cached Domain Credentials.

title: Credential material harvested from LSASS/SAM; no offline cracking observed
rationale: Describes LSASS and SAM handle access as credential harvesting; the technique assigned is Password Cracking per the finding, though cracking itself was not observed.

title: No password spraying; reused pbeesly credentials for lateral movement
rationale: Finding explicitly rules out spraying and attributes repeated logons to lateral movement with stolen credentials; technique retained as assigned.

title: WebDAV/UNC forced authentication to attacker server 192.168.0.4 from scranton
rationale: New-PSDrive to \\192.168.0.4\webdav with explicit credentials and DavClnt/401 WebDAV artifacts; forced authentication.

title: NASHUA python.exe beaconing to 192.168.0.4:8443 with self-signed TLS
rationale: Same external endpoint as the forced-auth WebDAV activity; assessed as credential-capture listener interaction. Best fit Forced Authentication.

title: Credential-harvesting tooling staged as .ps1 in SysinternalsSuite; no plaintext credential files read
rationale: Attacker scripts masquerading as Sysinternals content; no credential files read. Best fit Credentials In Files.

title: NASHUA: harvested password/login-named files into working.zip
rationale: Recursive enumeration of credential-bearing file patterns and archiving. Best fit Credentials In Files.

title: SCRANTON: unsigned .scr dropper launched by explorer.exe writing monkey.png payload
rationale: Initial dropper for credential-access tooling; technique retained as Credentials In Files per finding, though the action is execution/delivery.

title: SCRANTON: accesschk.exe permission reconnaissance from staged SysinternalsSuite
rationale: Permission reconnaissance supporting credential access; technique retained as Credentials In Files per finding.

title: Certificate/private-key export via Get-PrivateKeys to .pfx files on scranton
rationale: Same Get-PrivateKeys script block (readme.ps1) enumerating cert:\LocalMachine and Export-PfxCertificate to Downloads with password 'saribas'. Private key material theft.

title: SCRANTON: registry value read and Invoke-Expression'd, hostui.exe elevated
rationale: Registry value read and executed; no plaintext credential observed. Technique retained as Group Policy Preferences per finding.

title: SCRANTON: sdclt.exe UAC-bypass launcher followed by hidden steganographic PowerShell
rationale: Elevation/loader activity; no browser credential store read observed. Technique retained as Credentials from Web Browsers per finding, though unconfirmed.

title: Windows Vault / Credential Manager artifacts touched on scranton
rationale: vaultcli/vaultsvc loads and Vault Latest.dat deletion by lsass; low confidence, no vaultcmd usage. Best fit Windows Credential Manager.

title: Compromised host chain scranton→nashua with LSASS access; no Kerberos ticket theft observed
rationale: SeaDuke toolkit and LSASS access but no ticket theft/forgery; technique retained as Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets per finding.

title: Certificate harvesting followed by archive and exfiltration (scranton)
rationale: F19 covers the Get-PrivateKeys export plus Invoke-Exfil archiving and exfiltration; the credential-access action is stealing authentication certificates. F56 is separate (see below).

title: ROOT certificate store blob modification on nashua by Sysmon.exe
rationale: Single 4657 modification of a SystemCertificates ROOT blob; certificate-store tampering, low confidence, no corroborating forgery.
